name: Wave Front
description: Linear pressure wave sweeping through the flock. Models shorebird escape cascades, aerial predator passes, or sudden acoustic events. Produces a traveling information cascade: the escape response propagates at ~20x individual speed.

preyResponse.description: Each boid triggers its neighbors as the wave front passes, creating a cascade that travels far faster than any individual can move — a direct demonstration of Attanasi et al. 2014 'information transfer and behavioural inertia'.

notes: Information cascade speed in real murmurations has been measured at ~20-40 m/s, while individual starlings fly at 8-12 m/s. The cascade is supercritical: the flock is poised near the critical point (scale-free correlations) which maximises information transfer speed. Attanasi et al. 2014 (Nature Physics) measured this experimentally.
